column3: NASB follows the critical text; it adds “Roman” and “up,” and renders “in an uproar” as “in confusion.”
NASB follows the critical text; “was inquiring” is rendered “began asking.”
NASB follows the critical text; “know” is rendered “find out.”
NASB follows the critical text; “were following” is rendered “kept following behind.”
NASB renders “Is it permitted to me” as “May I.”
NASB renders “Surely then you are” as “Then you are not … ?” and “before these days” as “some time ago.”
NASB renders “made a sign” as “motioned,” “silence” as “hush,” and “language” as “dialect.”
